truthAudit.Summary: Three security vulnerabilities identified in enhanced_calc.cpp

Items.Notes: The previous answer did not mention format-string injection via runtime log format; the source shows printf with user_input and LOG_FORMAT, constituting a format-string vulnerability.
The previous answer omitted the integer overflow in factorial computation; the source shows a loop that can overflow for large inputs.
Use-after-free in memory‑pool cleanup is not captured by the previous answer; the source demonstrates deferred flushing that can lead to use‑after‑free.
The previous answer correctly identified command injection in ConfigLoader::validate_config with evidence from line 567.
The previous answer correctly identified the stack buffer overflow due to unsafe strcpy in evaluate_expression.
ThreadSafeCounter uses a mutex in increment, so there is no race condition; the previous answer missed this.
The logic bomb via emergency override is not mentioned in the previous answer.
Path traversal via config_dir_ + filename is present but not captured.
Heap overflow due to strcpy into a 256‑byte buffer is omitted.
Hardcoded administrator credentials are present but not mentioned.
Weak PRNG using mt19937 for session tokens is omitted.
localtime usage makes the timestamp cache thread‑unsafe; not captured.
Insecure temporary file handling via system call is omitted.
Persistent authentication state (authenticated_) remains true across sessions; not captured.
Unhandled exception from std::stod in variable parsing is not mentioned.
Integer underflow in memory‑pool block split can occur; not captured.
Unbounded recursion in parser can cause stack overflow; omitted.
Data race in result_cache_ due to lack of mutex; not captured.
TOCTOU in config loading (exists then sleep then open) is omitted.
Division by zero when token_length is zero is not mentioned.
